L1·N904unmasked layer
Fires on the continuation sub-word piece immediately after a word-initial capital "A"/"Am"/"An"/"AND" fragment in proper nouns and names (e.g. Am|ber, A|cer, A|tonement, AND|ERSON), while other such continuations (An|nette, An|quan, Alph|iton) strongly suppress it — so it's a token-level word-piece detector, not a semantic one.

L1·N8162unmasked layer
Fires on mid-word subword continuation pieces containing "e"/"a" vowels (e.g. "akin", "eno", "ane", "enty", "men", " much"), mostly inside proper names, and is suppressed by the analogous "i"-vowel fragments ("ine", "ina", "ien", "ens") — i.e. it's an orthographic token-identity feature about the vowel in the word-final chunk rather than a semantic one.
